title: Vegetables, stew type, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed vegetables with no added fat are a blend of various vegetables gently cooked in their own juices. Cooking without oil preserves the maximum amount of vitamins, minerals, and natural flavors, making the dish light and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stewing retains more fiber compared to frying.
Common ingredients include carrots, broccoli, bell peppers, and zucchini.
Stewed vegetables can serve as a base for soups, stews, and side dishes.
The absence of added fat reduces the calorie count, which is useful for diet plans.
Slow cooking keeps the vegetables’ natural color and aroma.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Vegetables provide vitamins A, C, K and B‑complex, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: They contain potassium, magnesium and iron, essential for heart and muscle function.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: No added fat makes the dish suitable for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in vegetables help combat free radicals.

items.title: Allergy to specific vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may react to certain vegetables such as tomatoes or peppers.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Excessive stewing can diminish heat‑sensitive vitamins like vitamin C.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Vegetables like spinach and beetroot are high in oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stones in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed vegetables can be served on their own, added to salads, used as a filling for wraps, or as a side to meat and fish. They reheat well in the microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked stewed vegetables in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before consumption.
